Implemented on branch `iam-titan-f10f`, commit `92c47154586` (Change-Id `I434df308687c03cbe456693954ba3363ed1e9cec`).

## Codebase AC evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Titan ARN listed in `bedrock_converse` | `arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` added to the resource list |
| Both Claude ARNs retained | foundation-model `anthropic.claude-*` and inference-profile `*.anthropic.claude-*` both present, unmodified |
| Exactly one statement | one `statement {` block in `data.aws_iam_policy_document.bedrock_converse` |
| Actions unchanged | `bedrock:InvokeModel`, `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` — byte-identical |
| sid no longer Claude-only | `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly` → `InvokeScopedBedrockModels` |
| header comment corrected | no longer says "Claude-only" or "constraining the Anthropic model"; now names both families |
| `bedrock-ci-oidc.md:130` unchanged | not in the diff; sole hunk is `@@ -145,2 +145,4 @@` plus a one-phrase fix at `:32` |
| `bedrock-ci-oidc.md:239` unchanged | not in the diff; content intact, shifted +2 lines by the `:145` hunk |
| `:145` no longer claims "verbatim in shape" | rewritten to "the same shape ... which additionally grants the `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` embedding ARN that external CI does not need" |
| ADR no longer says "exactly two resource ARNs" | deployment-precondition section rewritten |
| `terraform validate` | **exit 0** — "Success! The configuration is valid." |
| `terraform fmt -check -recursive` | **exit 0** |
| no `src/rebar/` file modified | `git diff --name-only \| grep ^src/rebar/` → empty |

## Scope added during implementation

A whole-tree sweep for the claims this change falsifies — rather than editing only the cited lines — found three more in `infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md` that my own change made false:

- `:40` "you have not shown the **Claude-only scope** binds" → "the scoped model list binds"
- `:120` heading "a **non-Claude** model must be DENIED" → "an **unlisted** model must be DENIED"
- `:129` "the policy is meant to permit `anthropic.claude-*` **only**" → names both admitted families, and notes `amazon.nova-pro-v1:0` is in neither so the negative control still holds

The documented negative control still works unchanged: it probes `amazon.nova-pro-v1:0`, which the widened policy still denies.

`bedrock-access.md` was added to `file_impact`. I verified empirically that this does **not** void the plan-review attestation — `review-plan --status` returned `ok: true, verdict: certified, currency_basis: file_impact` both before and after the edit. The signed manifest carries its dep set frozen at signing; a path added later is not in it.

The three remaining "Claude-only" mentions in `bedrock-ci-oidc.md` (`:32`, `:160`, `:305`) describe the **external-CI** OIDC role, whose grant was *not* widened. They are correct as written. `:32` had said "the same Claude-only grant", which became false once the two policies diverged; reworded to "a Claude-only Bedrock grant of the same shape".

## Honesty note carried into the artifacts

Both the ADR and the commit message state that the grant is **declared, not confirmed live**: bug `1c39-96d4-8f9e-4d38` records that `iam_s7.tf` has not been verified as applied, and a policy simulator cannot settle it because Converse authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel` while the distinct `bedrock:Converse` action simulates as denied.

## Remaining

The `[non-codebase]` AC — an operator applying the Terraform and attesting the Titan call succeeds from the instance role — is outstanding and cannot be met from this session. `make verify` has not yet run on this branch (deferred to avoid contending with the `47c8` verify on the same host).

## The code half is merged

Commit `213341e3e58faf021f51ddd7db0285f57d95f2b9` ("Grant Titan embedding ARN to Bedrock policy") is an ancestor of `origin/main` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` exits 0). Verified against the merged tree, not the branch:

```
$ git show origin/main:infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf | grep -n 'titan\|sid'
12:    sid = "InvokeScopedBedrockModels"
20:      "arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0",
```

Both the Titan ARN and the renamed sid are live in `main`. All 14 codebase acceptance criteria are therefore satisfied in the merged tree, and the earlier comment's "`make verify` has not yet run on this branch" is superseded: the change passed CI's `Verified` gate as a condition of merging.

## What is left

Only the `[non-codebase]` criterion: an operator applies the Terraform and records an attestation here carrying the Gerrit change number, the revision SHA, the UTC timestamp, the dimension count from a real Titan embedding call made from the Gerrit instance role, and the operator identity.

That is an AWS apply plus a live credential-bearing call. It cannot be performed or attested from an agent session, and the ticket's own Approach section explains why no substitute exists: `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` is not fired by a Gerrit change, applies run manually through `scripts/terraform_prod.py`, and a policy simulator cannot settle it because Converse authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel` while the distinct `bedrock:Converse` action simulates as denied.

The ticket stays `in_progress` pending that attestation. Note that it is not a feature blocker: the lexical tier needs no model provider, and the embedding tier is unset by default and degrades to lexical when the provider is absent or denies.

## Context / Problem

The Gerrit instance role cannot invoke the Titan embedding model. `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` grants `bedrock:InvokeModel` and `bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream` (`:11-14`) against exactly two Anthropic Claude ARNs (`:15-18`). The sibling embedding story's opt-in tier calls Titan from that role, and the call is denied.

This task widens that one statement so the configured default works in this deployment. It is not a feature blocker: the lexical tier the sibling index story builds requires no model provider at all, so similar-ticket retrieval works without this change everywhere, including here.

## Approach

### Widen the existing statement

The single statement at `iam_s7.tf:9-19` gains the Titan embedding model ARN alongside its two Claude ARNs. The actions already include `bedrock:InvokeModel` (`:12`), which is what Bedrock authorizes an embedding call against, so no action is added.

A second statement is not introduced. The two grants share one role, one action set and one purpose — invoking a scoped set of Bedrock models — and splitting them would double the surface a reader must check to answer what this role can invoke.

### Rename the sid

The sid is `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly` (`:10`). Once the statement grants a non-Anthropic model, that name is false, and a false sid is worse than a vague one because it is the string an auditor reads to decide whether the grant matches its description. It is renamed to describe what the statement actually permits: invoking a scoped set of Bedrock models.

The header comment (`:1-6`) carries the same claim in prose — "a Claude-only Bedrock policy" (`:1`) and "constraining the Anthropic model" (`:4`) — and is corrected with it.

### The runbook's sid occurrences belong to a different role, and are left alone

`infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md` contains the same sid string twice, and **neither occurrence is this role**:

- `:130` sits inside a JSON block the runbook introduces at `:123` as inline policy `rebar-external-ci-bedrock-converse`.
- `:239` is `data "aws_iam_policy_document" "external_ci_bedrock_converse"`, attached at `:251-254` to role `gha_external_ci_bedrock`, tagged `Ticket = "f124"` (`:233`).

Both describe the external-CI OIDC role, whose resources (`:245-246`) are Claude-only and stay Claude-only — it does not call Titan. The runbook justifies that restriction at `:158-159` as "the least-privilege oracle", and that justification remains true for that role. Renaming its sid would make an accurately-named grant describe a widening it never received, and editing the `:130` JSON would change the policy operators are instructed to create in AWS.

So both occurrences are left exactly as they are.

### The claim that actually breaks

`:145` states the JSON block is "`iam_s7.tf`'s `aws_iam_policy_document.bedrock_converse`, verbatim in shape." Adding the Titan ARN to `iam_s7.tf` makes that false, and no sid edit can repair it — the two resource lists diverge. That sentence is rewritten to state the relationship that is true afterwards: the same shape as `iam_s7.tf`'s statement, which additionally grants the Titan embedding ARN.

This is the only runbook edit.

### ADR 0122's ARN count

`docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md:184` states the statement "lists exactly two resource ARNs (`:15-18`)". That citation is accurate today and this change falsifies the count, so the sentence is updated here rather than left for a reader to trip over.

### Applied state is not assumed

No Gerrit gate applies this Terraform, so this task's Terraform claims are "declared", not "live". `.github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml` triggers on `pull_request`, a daily `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` — none of which a Gerrit change fires — and its own header states it "does not contribute to the Gerrit Verified label". Applies are manual, via `scripts/terraform_prod.py`. A policy simulator cannot settle it either: Converse authorizes against `bedrock:InvokeModel` while `bedrock:Converse` exists as a distinct simulatable action that simulates as denied, as `infra/runbooks/bedrock-access.md` records. Only a real call proves access, which is why the operator attestation below is a separate, explicitly non-codebase criterion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf`'s `bedrock_converse` statement lists the Titan embedding model ARN. Checked by: reading the resource list.
- [x] That statement still lists both Claude ARNs present before this change. Checked by: reading the resource list.
- [x] `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` contains exactly one statement in `data.aws_iam_policy_document.bedrock_converse`. Checked by: reading the document block.
- [x] The statement's actions are unchanged from before this change. Checked by: diffing the actions list.
- [x] The statement's sid does not assert an Anthropic-only or Claude-only restriction. Checked by: reading the sid.
- [x] The header comment at `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:1-6` does not describe the policy as Claude-only or Anthropic-constrained. Checked by: reading the comment.
- [x] `infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md:130` is unchanged. Checked by: the change's diff not touching that line.
- [x] `infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md:239` is unchanged. Checked by: the change's diff not touching that line.
- [x] `infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md` no longer claims the documented external-CI policy is `iam_s7.tf`'s statement verbatim in shape. Checked by: reading the sentence at the `:145` location.
- [x] That same sentence states that `iam_s7.tf`'s statement additionally grants the Titan embedding ARN. Checked by: reading it.
- [x] `docs/adr/0122-similar-ticket-retrieval.md` no longer states the statement lists exactly two resource ARNs. Checked by: reading the sentence at the `:184` location.
- [x] `terraform validate` exits 0 against `infra/terraform/`. Checked by: running it.
- [x] `terraform fmt -check` exits 0 against `infra/terraform/`. Checked by: running it.
- [x] No file under `src/rebar/` is modified. Checked by: the change's diff.
- [ ] `[non-codebase]` An operator applies this Terraform and records an attestation on this ticket containing the Gerrit change number, the revision SHA, the UTC timestamp, the dimension count returned by a real Titan embedding call from the Gerrit instance role, and the operator's identity. Checked by: the comment being present on this ticket.
